extra.message: The `host` query parameter of GET /ops/shell/ticket-probe-699 is concatenated directly into a shell command executed with os.system(). An attacker who can reach this endpoint can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id) to execute arbitrary OS commands as the application user.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: The `fragment` query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string that is then compiled and rendered. Jinja2 template syntax supplied by the attacker is evaluated server-side, which allows sandbox escape and arbitrary Python code execution (e.g. fragment={{ self.__init__.__globals__ }}).

cwe: CWE-94: Code Injection

extra.message: The `packet_ref` query parameter is joined onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR without canonicalisation or confinement, then the raw request body is written to it. A value such as packet_ref=../../../../home/app/.ssh/authorized_keys escapes the export directory and writes attacker-controlled bytes to an arbitrary filesystem path.

cwe: CWE-22: Path Traversal

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/ticket-shelf-726 builds the destination path from the externally controlled `name` parameter with no path normalisation or allowlist, then calls mkdir(parents=True) and write_bytes(). Traversal sequences in `name` let an attacker create directories and overwrite arbitrary files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR.

cwe: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path

extra.message: The request body is parsed with an lxml XMLParser explicitly configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. This enables XML external entity processing, allowing local file disclosure (SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd") and outbound SSRF from the parser.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: POST /api/auth/reset-password is unauthenticated and accepts `email`, `token` and `new_password`, but the supplied `token` is never validated (the code only carries a comment 'In production, verify token'). Any anonymous attacker can set the password of any account, including support_admin, and fully take it over.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded literal 'change-me-in-production-local-dev-only' when the environment variable is unset. Because this value is committed in source, anyone with repository access can forge HS256 JWTs for any user id and role and bypass authentication entirely (get_current_user trusts the 'sub' claim).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: GET /ops/badge/ticket-gate-689 decides whether to return elevated data (payroll, open casework) based on the client-supplied `ops_badge` cookie or `x-ops-badge` header. Privilege is asserted by the client rather than derived from authoritative server-side identity, so any caller can send ops_badge=lead to obtain the elevated response.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: POST /ops/workset/ticket-rebind-206 builds a server-side workset with security-relevant defaults (role, tier, approved, balance) and then applies the entire untrusted JSON body over it with dict.update(). An attacker can set role='admin', approved=true or an arbitrary balance, so client input directly overwrites privilege attributes.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: GET /ops/fold/ticket-agent-file-120 is the only route in this operations router that omits the `_wrk_gate` dependency, so it requires no token and no user session, yet it returns internal ticket counts and an ops memo describing 'renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details'. Any anonymous caller can read this internal data.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The `lane` query parameter is passed straight into RedirectResponse with no allowlist or same-origin check, so /ops/after/ticket-lane-165?lane=https://evil.example redirects the victim to an attacker-chosen site, enabling phishing and token leakage via the destination.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: The `card` query parameter is rendered through a Jinja2 template that applies the `|safe` filter, disabling autoescaping, and the result is returned as an HTMLResponse. Supplying card=<script>...</script> yields reflected cross-site scripting in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Cross-site Scripting

extra.message: The full request body and the raw `Authorization` header are written to the application log at WARNING level. Bearer tokens and any credentials or PII in the body are persisted in plaintext log files, exposing them to anyone with log access and enabling session replay.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: A user-supplied phrase (defaulting to 'welcome', i.e. credential-like material) is digested with MD5. MD5 is collision-prone, unsalted here, and extremely fast to brute-force, so the resulting digest offers no meaningful protection for the input value.

cwe: CWE-328: Use of Weak Hash

extra.message: A nonce/code returned to callers is generated with random.choice(), which uses the deterministic Mersenne Twister PRNG rather than the `secrets` module. An attacker who observes a few outputs can recover the generator state and predict subsequent security tokens.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The outbound partner request is made with ssl._create_unverified_context(), which disables certificate chain and hostname verification. Any network attacker can transparently man-in-the-middle this HTTPS call and tamper with the partner status response.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: The identity-hint endpoint authenticates handles against a hardcoded dictionary of static verifier values ({'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}) committed in source. These shared secrets cannot be rotated, are visible to anyone with repo access, and are short numeric PINs.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The verifier check on /ops/identity/ticket-hint-659 has no rate limiting, throttling, delay, or lockout — there is no such middleware anywhere in the FastAPI app (see backend/app/main.py:56 where only CORSMiddleware is registered). The 4-digit verifier space can be exhausted in a few thousand requests.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: POST /api/auth/login performs an unlimited number of password verifications per account with no rate limiting, account lockout, CAPTCHA, or progressive delay. Only CORSMiddleware is installed on the app (main.py:56) and no gateway limiter exists in the repo, so credential stuffing and password brute-force against any account are unimpeded. The same applies to /api/auth/forgot-password and /api/auth/reset-password.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Successful logins are recorded with audit_log(db, 'login', ...) at main.py:83, but failed authentication attempts raise HTTP 401 with no audit record, and there is no AuditAction enum member for a login failure (backend/app/models.py:52-75). Authorization failures raised by require_roles (backend/app/auth.py:104-108) are likewise never logged, and no middleware or exception handler supplies this. Credential-stuffing and privilege-probing campaigns therefore leave no durable trace.

cwe: CWE-778: Insufficient Logging

extra.message: PUT /api/escalations/{escalation_id} loads the escalation by id and applies the update with no scope check, unlike list_escalations (main.py:636-638) which restricts a team_lead to escalations on their own teams' tickets. Any team_lead can therefore resolve, reject, or reassign the ownership of an escalation belonging to another team's ticket by supplying its id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: PUT /api/tickets/{ticket_id} is open to require_any (including customer_user) and gates only on _authorize_ticket, which for a customer merely compares organization_id. Every field of TicketUpdate — including status, priority, assignee_id and team_id (backend/app/schemas.py:243-250) — is then blindly setattr'd. A customer can modify any co-worker's ticket, reassign it to an arbitrary agent, move it to another team, or mark it resolved.

cwe: CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: The entire upload directory is mounted as a public StaticFiles route at /uploads with no authentication or authorization dependency, bypassing the ownership checks that /api/attachments/{id}/download performs (main.py:611-623). Any anonymous request for a known or leaked stored filename retrieves the attachment content directly.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The customer CSV import creates every new customer_user account with the hardcoded password 'changeme123' and there is no forced-reset flag on the User model. An attacker who knows this constant (it is committed in source) can log in as any imported customer before they first authenticate.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The session cookie holding the JWT is set without the `secure` attribute, so the browser will transmit it over plaintext HTTP. A network attacker able to downgrade or observe an HTTP request to the origin can capture the access token and hijack the session.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: This response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and blanks the Content-Security-Policy header, actively turning off browser-side protections. Combined with the reflected-XSS sinks in the same router (lines 70 and 92), this removes the defence-in-depth that would otherwise limit script execution.

cwe: CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: The application entrypoint unconditionally starts uvicorn with reload=True and binds 0.0.0.0, with no environment guard to disable the reloader outside development. The auto-reload watcher is development-only functionality that adds a filesystem-watching child process and re-executes code on file change; shipping it as the production start path (scripts/run_backend.sh invokes this file) leaves active debug functionality enabled.

cwe: CWE-489: Active Debug Code

extra.message: GET /api/dashboard/stats is exposed to require_any (customer_user included) but computes counts over the whole Ticket table with no organization_id scoping, unlike list_tickets (main.py:290-291). A customer of one organization learns global ticket volume, overdue and escalation counts, and average resolution time across every other tenant.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
